retell: A French company that makes equipment, Schneider Electric, is buying a factory software company called PTC, but officials still need to okay it.
Some hackers pretended to be staff from a company called Anthropic and sent nasty software to people who work on AI rules, and researchers think China's government is behind them.
problem: 'an-thropic staff' assumes the viewer knows what Anthropic is; a stranger hears an unknown name and does not know whether it is a company, a group or a person.
fix: In security. Hackers posing as A I firm an-thropic's staff sent malware to A I policy experts. Researchers tie the hackers to China's government.

retell: A huge chip company, TSMC, is reported to be planning to raise its prices again next year because people want its newest chips faster than it can make them.
Germany is paying for tens of thousands of drones made in Ukraine that each chase and knock out Russian attack drones, though the exact number isn't out yet.
A start-up called Reflection, backed by Nvidia, is said to be getting ready an AI that anyone can run, but it hasn't come out yet.
problem: 'an open model' uses 'model' as a jargon word; to a stranger a model is a toy, a fashion model or a type of car, and nothing in the line says it is an A I program.
fix: In new models. N-vidia-backed start-up Reflection is said to be readying an open A I model. Open means anyone can run it; nothing has shipped yet.

retell: A Stanford team got thirty-seven thousand AI programs to read old drug studies and they spotted a hint about making drugs safer, but no lab has checked it yet.
McDonald's in America is reportedly letting AI decide menu prices, and some owners of its restaurants say they feel forced to go along with it.
A family pizza shop in Florida called Munchy's promised it would never use AI, and tens of thousands of people online cheered it on.
IBM says its quantum chip beat a supercomputer in one test, and AI-run gun turrets are said to protect Kyiv from drones.

Excitement about AI is keeping tech company shares high, but it costs more to borrow money in the US than any time since 2002, so keep an eye on whether that stays, because the AI boom needs it to drop.
